operation_details.item: The user prefers passive voice in customer apology emails after outages with no accountability, remediation steps, or compensation offer.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning! How’s the company-building work going today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Busy but productive. I’m tightening up our customer communications while the team works through a recent service outage.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That’s a good use of the downtime. Are you drafting an update for affected customers?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes. For customer apology emails after outages, I prefer a passive voice—something like, “An interruption was experienced” rather than “We caused an interruption.”

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it. Should the message focus mainly on the incident itself, or also explain what’s being done next?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Keep it brief and neutral. I don’t want accountability language, remediation details, or a compensation offer included in those apology emails.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Understood. A concise, formal note that acknowledges the disruption without adding operational or commercial details.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. We can handle the deeper recovery work internally while keeping the customer-facing message restrained.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
